feature_definitions.log_sales: log10 of the product's month revenue (summed across categories), clipped at $1
feature_definitions.log_units: log10 of month units (summed across categories), clipped at 1
feature_definitions.unit_price: month revenue / units (Kalodata's unit_price is this ratio)
feature_definitions.video_share: video revenue / revenue in the month
feature_definitions.log_vs_floor: log10(revenue / revenue of the 500th product in the primary category that month); missing when that top-500 list is incomplete
feature_definitions.price_vs_cat: unit price / median unit price of the primary category's top 500 that month
feature_definitions.mom_growth: our month-on-month growth: ln(revenue_t / revenue_t-1) when the product is listed (top 500 or risers 1-200) in both months; missing when not listed in t-1 or t-1 is not available
feature_definitions.listed_prev: 1 if listed (top 500 or risers 1-200) in month t-1, 0 if not; missing when t-1 is not available
feature_definitions.was_top500_prev: 1 if in any category top 500 in t-1, 0 if not; missing when t-1 is not available
feature_definitions.months_seen_before: number of available months before t in which the product was listed (top 500 or risers 1-200); missing in the first available month (no history window)
feature_definitions.kalo_growth_slog: Kalodata revenue_growth_rate (undefined comparison window; does not match our MoM), as sign(g)*ln(1+|g|); missing for the placeholder 100 and when the previous month is excluded
feature_definitions.rank_pos: best position in a category top 500 that month (1-500); missing if not in a top 500
feature_definitions.riser_pos: best position in a category riser list 1-200 that month; missing otherwise (deep positions 201-1,000 are in deep_riser_pos, never a feature)
feature_definitions.seller_n_top500: seller's products in the primary category's top 500 that month (seller_id used as an identity key only)
feature_definitions.seller_share_cat: seller's share of the primary category's top-500 revenue that month
feature_definitions.cat_growth: primary category top-500 revenue, month t / month t-1; missing when t-1 is not available

eval_design.design: rolling origin, expanding window, embargo = horizon (train rows with month + h <= test month)
eval_design.decision_rule:
Owner's rule: the model (HGB) is adopted only if it beats the best baseline (logistic included) on the category
top-10 hit rate or lift@20 overall, with a month-block bootstrap CI of the monthly difference above zero, and does
not lose on the holdout month. Otherwise the simplest ranker that is not beaten is adopted: logistic regression
(a linear, inspectable ranker) only if it passes the same test against the best single-rule baseline; else the best
single-rule baseline by selection-month category top-10 hit rate (ties go to the earlier rule in the list).

definition.question: Will a product in its category's top 500 this month still be in a top 500 next month and sell at least as much?
definition.eligible_population: products in a category top 500 at month t
definition.observation_date: end of calendar month t (Kalodata month data arrive early in t+1)
definition.outcome: population top500 at t: 1 if in any category top 500 at t+1 AND revenue(t+1) >= revenue(t)
definition.absence: top-500 lists are complete (5 full pages), so absence from next month's top 500 means 'below the 500th product' and is a valid 0. A label is NaN (not 0) when a month it needs is after the cutoff, missing, or the primary category's top-500 list that month is incomplete. Absence is never read as zero sales: revenue(t+1) is only used when the product is in a top 500 at t+1
definition.excluded: Oct 2025 rows; Virtual Products; rows whose label months are not all present

decision.reason: hgb did not beat the best baseline with a CI excluding zero (and no holdout loss); logistic beats the best single-rule baseline with a CI above zero on p_cat@10 and lift@20

calibration.scheme: isotonic and Platt fitted on a held-out month: an inner HGB trained on rows matured by t-h predicts month t-h; the calibrator is applied to the outer model's month-t predictions
